items.oracle: Count 2 observations in first bin, 2 second, 1 third, 2 fourth, 2 fifth; total 9.

items.prompt: Data 0,1,2,5,6,7,8,9,11,12,20. Which bin 0–4,5–9,10–14,15–19,20–24 has the unique greatest frequency?
items.oracle: Frequencies 3,5,2,0,1; unique maximum is 5 in second bin.

items.prompt: A scores 17,19,20,0,2,3; B scores 16,18,21,22,23,1. Which class has more scores 15–24?
items.oracle: A=3, B=5 observations in upper two bins.

items.prompt: Can squares (0,0),(0,1),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1) fold into a cube without overlap?
items.oracle: Connected six-square net yields six unique consistent outward normals.

items.prompt: Can squares (0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(0,4),(1,0) fold into a cube without overlap?
items.oracle: The five-square straight run produces repeated face normals after folding.
